_about: The invasion's domains (decided 9 October; bible section 9). The other world is a JRPG world and the rift is where its overworld pushes into ours: a domain is one biome of the classic overworld, its bleed (the tileset the flattened ground paints, DomainGround's: plains, sand, marsh or lava), its wildlife with one tactical signature, and its hero. A rift rolls its domain when it opens, one lead and at most one guest. A pack on the battlefield is one composition on one hex: one sprite (its lead's), one badge (its count), its members listed on a tap (the foes' fresh start, 30 October). compositions are the packs the rift places and sends (the domain's shape on the map), each {id, size, tiers, front, back}, one grid declaration (Ryan, 8 November: the members and the layout one thing): size is patrol (one or two front types, three to five foes, a detachment's fight), formation (a front and a back, six to sixteen by the tier, the body's fight and the unit the Fractures are counted in), elite (led by a foe flagged elite, the guaranteed curveball a Fracture spawns) or escort (a boss's curated escort at a tier, never grown by the tier, a boss with none standing alone; one may name its boss, the boss's own coming first: the King Gel's Gels, which its merge takes in, 30 October); tiers lists the tiers (1 to 3) that may deal it, and a tier with none of a size has none, nothing standing in (every domain writes every size at every tier); front and back are the fight's two ranks, four cells each left to right as it stands, each cell null for empty or a foe id: a front-rank foe in a front cell, a back-rank foe in a back cell, a massive foe in a front cell with the back cell behind it null (it fills its column), a core's parts each in its own cell beside it (every part of every core in the grid, once a core); the pack is what the grid holds, the fight stands it so, and the grid is the whole declaration, no count beside it (a variant with one more goblin is its own composition: Ryan, 7 November, discrete variants placed on the tier and the ramp). Four fields more, each optional (the long wall brief, docs/briefs/long_wall_build.md 3.7; the ramp gate, 7 November; hunts, 8 November): squad, the machines it is intended for, 1 to 4, shown on the map as its threat rating, a patrol reading 1, a formation 3, an elite and an escort 4 where it names none (Ryan, 6 November); lead, a foe id in the grid, the pack's sprite, its elite in an elite composition, the first foe in reading order (front left to right, then back) leading where it names none; hunts, whether the pack hunts and whom, its caveat (nearest, weakest, strongest or slowest), the composition's to say and never its foes' (Ryan, 8 November: "The composition should say if it hunts, not the units"), never on an escort, which walks with its boss (absent: the pack pushes for the wall); ramp, [lo, hi], the Convergences it is dealt at (absent: every one), a tier's gated compositions of a size together holding every Convergence the tier is fought at. The spawn lists by tier are derived (ContentDB.spawn_table: the tier's formations' then patrols' members, each foe once, first seen first) for the harness, the runners and a boss's escort; boss lists the domain's bosses (bible section 9: a named JRPG entity each, three a domain before its hero and more welcome (Ryan, 3 November), each battle drawing one its domain has not ended on this run; the slate's twelve, 30 October, the old massive stand-ins gone to the rank and file and the Bone Wyvern to the elites; the Malboro, the Tonberry and the Adamantoise out of the lists 3 November, species rather than named entities, the Mantis Ant the Meadow's third and the Marsh Serpent the Marsh's fourth since 4 November, the Emperor Scorpion the Waste's third); bench names the heroes the campaign's start may deal to this domain, one per campaign, the domain's final (the party, bible section 9: the hero stands in its rank with the domain's wildlife in the other columns). opening, true on one domain at most, marks the one a run opens against (Ryan, 19 November: the first battle is the Meadow's, fought by the draft's three machines, so that domain's first battle alone is sized for a trio): until the run's first battle is fought every rift that opens is its; with none marked the first rifts roll as any other. A domain names no map shape: a battle draws its shape by its seed (Ryan, 30 October: "I don't see why the domain should be related to the map type in any way"). Shown to the player: name, flavour. design is internal and never shown: fantasy, signature (what the domain does), answer (how the player beats it, in the engine's own vocabulary). A patrol's and a formation's own design holds its question (what the player must answer, required, the formation pass of 10 November) and, where a member stands outside its role, the crossing's reason; the validator holds a formation to pushers, a patrol that pushes to flankers, and a pack that hunts to a hunter's lead and what keeps its pace. Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: The Meadow

design.fantasy: The first overworld: grass, round trees, a road that goes nowhere. The invasion's shallow end, and the first thing CARE ever classified. Dragon Quest's plains and Final Fantasy's, where the slime and the goblin live.
design.signature: Numbers that split and swarm. Dumb and many.
design.answer: Area damage, armour against volume, kill order.

design.question: Eight: four knives behind scrap shields and four screamers behind them, every column walled. Area on the front, then the back; every screamer lashes corruption onto what a machine shows and leaves its killer Brittle as it is pulled up, so time the root kills to stop the corruption bleed, or clear the goblins first so the Brittle has no knives behind it (Ryan, 20 November: "there's at least a nugget of strategy that stops it from being kill frontline-kill backline in that order").

The treant fills its column and regrows what you cut; two screamers stand behind the goblins, each leaving its killer Brittle as it dies: open a hole to reach one, and decide whether the tree or the back goes first.

Three gels split into six halves and hold the line, every Engulf leaving its machine Ablating, so spread the hits so they do not stack (Ryan, 20 November); the screamers behind lash while they do, and each one killed leaves its killer Brittle. The stacks grow while the wall stands, so its cost is its length: area clears the halves, Indirect reaches past them.
A duel for one machine: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land. What is left showing, and is the best die spent first?
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land. What is left showing, and is the best die spent first?
Four wolves pounce on the slowest machine and howl each other on: keep the slow one in company, or kill two before the howls stack.
Eight, every column walled: four braced knives and four screamers.

The dusk treant regrows four and below half its roots come up under every machine: shield the storm, burst past the regen, while the guards' plate costs the time you need and every mandrake pulled leaves the whole team Brittle.

Bad Breath lays Ablating, Scorched, a jam and a corruption on every machine at once (a Cleanse, or a Ward); below half it seeds two mandragoras into the open ground behind. Kill it before it seeds, or kill what it seeds.

Bubble gels leave every machine they flow over Brittle, so the blows after land harder, and split into halves that do the same; the mandrakes behind leave the whole team Brittle as they fall. Spread the hits, and kill the gels before the stack lands. A placeholder until tier two is sized.

Two anchors: the bloom's breath and the treant's root storm, each a telegraph, behind two braced guards, with the mandrakes leaving the whole team Brittle as they fall. Which anchor first is the fight.
A duel for one machine: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land. What is left showing, and is the best die spent first?
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land. What is left showing, and is the best die spent first?
Wargs run down the weakest machine on the field: the hurt one is the prey, so it fights in company or alone to the death.

Two captains in the line shout the warband harder each round, the warchief behind them names one machine for the whole warband to turn on, and two alraunes behind the guards turn the die's shown entry to wood: stop the pointing, silence the shouting or reach the back, past braced knives.

Two molten gels and a bubble gel, every Engulf leaving Brittle and the molten ones Ablating too, while the captain rallies and the alraunes jam: spread the hits so they do not stack, or burn the gels down first. A placeholder until tier three is sized (the Metal Gel's drift until 20 November).
The frost treant regrows five and its roots come up under everyone below half; the alraunes behind the guards jam what you show.
The frost treant and the bloom side by side, a captain shouting in the line and an alraune jamming behind it: two telegraphs, a rally and a jam, the Meadow at its densest.
A duel for one machine: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land. What is left showing, and is the best die spent first?
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land. What is left showing, and is the best die spent first?

One alpha marks the weakest machine and howls three wargs onto it: the alpha first, or the pack (Ryan, 20 November: "If the pack was one alpha and a bunch of lessers, then there's at least a game plan").
A pack for one machine at the wall's end: two screamers and no screen. Each lash corrupts what the die shows, so take them before the die is needed elsewhere.
A pack for one: a knife and the screamer behind it. The goblin first opens the column, the screamer first stops the corruption.
A pack for one: two knives that wall each other and stab only shielded. One gauge ends them if nothing is wasted on the wall.
A pack for one: a gel alone. Its halves step up as it falls and every Engulf stacks Ablating on the one machine there, so end it fast or bring a second.
The duel for one machine, once the squad has grown into it: its whiskers switch off the entry the die is showing as they land.
The duel before the squad has grown into it, a pack for two: one machine takes the whiskers, the other the kill.
A pack for two: three knives walling each other. Two machines end it in two rounds; one alone pays a reboot.
A pack for two: two knives, two screamers behind them. Which column opens first, and who carries the corruption?
A pack for two: two gels, four halves to come. Spread the Engulfs across two hulls, or one machine wears all the Ablating.
A pack for two: one treant, slow, plated, regrowing what is cut. It can be left to walk while the faster packs are met, or cut down by a pair before it reaches the wall.
A pack for two: four knives, every one walled by its neighbours. An area gun's fight, a long one without it.
The duel doubled, a pack for two: each machine loses the entry its die shows as the whiskers land.
A pack for three down the middle: three knives behind scrap shields, three screamers behind them. Area on the front, then the back, and time the root kills to stop the corruption.
A pack for three down the middle, slow: a treant, two knives and a screamer. The tree or the small ones first, while it regrows what is cut.
The horde a head heavier: four knives, three screamers. A reboot for one machine of the three, or an area gun spares it.
A pack for three: a wall of gels with two screamers behind it. Six halves to come, and the Ablating wants spreading across three hulls.
The horde whole: four knives, four screamers, every column walled. A reboot each for three machines, and no fight for two.
The grove whole, slow: the treant, three knives, two screamers behind them. Open a hole to reach a screamer and decide whether the tree or the back goes first.
A pack for three, slow: two treants, plated, each regrowing what is cut. Big single shots, one tree at a time.

entries.flavour: Gate order one: if it is green and it is coming at you, it is not grass.

entries.name: The Waste

design.fantasy: Desert and badlands: sand, dunes, bleached bones, and cacti in rows all facing the same way. The genre's fixed-damage country, where the needles go through whatever you put up and the thieves take what you have.
design.signature: Needles and great bites that purge before they land, so nothing a machine puts up answers them; theft of entries and of buffs.
design.answer: Hull and tempo over what you put up; redundancy on the die against theft; reach to the gazers; a Ward.

design.question: Eight: four needlers and four stares, every column walled.
The worm bites hard and digs in when hurt, three plate until it acts again: hit it when it is not dug in, while the needlers cost hull.
A duel for one machine: it climbs, and a round later it stoops. A Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands?
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: it climbs, and a round later it stoops. A Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands?
Three antlions on the slowest machine.
Barbs that corrupt the entry you show, basilisks that stone your guns, and a djinn that unmakes your buffs: the Waste's whole hand, every piece behind a needler.
The night worm bites hard, digs in when hurt and heaves the ground under everyone below half.
Two djinns unmake the buffs on the machine that carries the most, and hide in a mirage when hurt: buff late, or kill them first.
A duel for one machine: it climbs, and a round later it stoops. A Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands?
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: it climbs, and a round later it stoops. A Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands?
Two pit antlions wait for the slowest machine: heavy jaws and a barrier when hurt.
Two great needlers gather for two rounds and loose every needle at once: kill them, suppress them or shield their picks; the gorgons corrupt what you show.
Two djinns and two gorgons behind the barbs: your buffs unmade and your shown entry corrupted or stoned every round. Play unbuffed with a second weapon, or reach the back.
The salt worm, oldest of its line, with three gatherers beside it and two gorgons behind them.
A duel for one machine: it climbs, and a round later it stoops. A Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands?
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: it climbs, and a round later it stoops. A Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands?
The queen and two pits wait for the slowest machine: her Devour feeds her three back a bite, barriers when hurt.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix K: the cactus has never been seen to move. Do not take your eyes off the cactus.

entries.name: The Marsh

design.fantasy: Swamp, graveyard, the dungeon: dead trees, tombstones, the poison swamp's purple. The genre's undead, in rusted ornate plate, with the healer who heals them standing behind.
design.signature: Hard to keep down: they regrow, get back up and are called again.
design.answer: Kill order and reach (the healer behind), burst that beats regrow.

design.question: Eight: four claws and four raisers, every column walled.
The giant knits three a round for three rounds once hurt: burst it or purge the mending; the ghosts refill the line.
Knights ready themselves once hurt and get back up whole: take one from full to dead in a round, or kill the ghosts that raise the rest.
A duel for one machine: hurt, it readies its rise and gets back up once. Burst it before it readies, purge the rise, or keep the big die for the second life.
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: hurt, it readies its rise and gets back up once. Burst it before it readies, purge the rise, or keep the big die for the second life.
Wights knit when hurt and spectres strip the marks you lay and raise the dead: kill a wight whole, cash a mark before the spectre acts, and reach the back.
The grave giant knits and, once hurt, readies itself to get back up whole: a wall of regeneration that wants burst.
The knights' grave guard plates every foe through the next round: time your blows outside it; each knight gets up once.
A duel for one machine: hurt, it readies its rise and gets back up once. Burst it before it readies, purge the rise, or keep the big die for the second life.
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: hurt, it readies its rise and gets back up once. Burst it before it readies, purge the rise, or keep the big die for the second life.
The lich readies its own to rise once and the dread knights strike as they fall, behind two draugr that knit: kill order is the fight, the lich first, a shield up before each knight dies.
The charnel giant knits four and gets back up once; the wraiths corrupt, raise and cleanse behind the draugr.
Two grave guards plating the line by turns and four raisers behind it, two of them corrupting: time the blows between the guards, kill the choir before the line refills.
The lich behind readies the draugr to get back up, and they knit while they stand: reach the lich first, or burst each draugr and be ready to do it twice.
A duel for one machine: hurt, it readies its rise and gets back up once. Burst it before it readies, purge the rise, or keep the big die for the second life.
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: hurt, it readies its rise and gets back up once. Burst it before it readies, purge the rise, or keep the big die for the second life.

entries.flavour: Gate order four: nothing that has died passes the wall. Nothing.

entries.name: The Peak

design.fantasy: Volcano and mountain, the fire cave: lava, black rock, the orange. The genre's bombs and drakes, furious rather than evil, and the mage who throws fire for a living.
design.signature: Hard hits on a telegraph, and heat.
design.answer: Shields for the telegraph, cooling, a lure onto a cold machine.

design.question: Eight: four drakes behind the pit.

The elemental's fist lands every round and, hurt, its cracks vent on everyone: plate answers the fist, cooling the vent; two drakes behind the lizards stoke, and a hurt bomb shows its burst a round ahead.
A duel for one machine: three bites at once strip a shield a Barrier cannot save, or one scorching maul it can. Read which is coming, and mind the heat the maul leaves.
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: three bites at once strip a shield a Barrier cannot save, or one scorching maul it can. Read which is coming, and mind the heat the maul leaves.
The wyverns dive for half again their bite, the spike a Barrier or a shield is sized for; the lizards scorch three a bite.
Grenades burst on every machine once hurt: kill them whole, suppress them, or shield everyone.
The basalt stokes every other foe harder and its fist lands hard; below half it vents on everyone; a wyvern dives from behind the lizards.
A duel for one machine: three bites at once strip a shield a Barrier cannot save, or one scorching maul it can. Read which is coming, and mind the heat the maul leaves.
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: three bites at once strip a shield a Barrier cannot save, or one scorching maul it can. Read which is coming, and mind the heat the maul leaves.
Two dragons go for the hottest machine, crush a round ahead and scorch everyone; the lizard primes the pack to ablate. Cool, shield the crush, kill the balloon whole.
Two primers in front of two dragons: every blow leaves you ablating while they stand.
Balloons swell a round and burst on everyone, scorching: one round to kill each whole, suppress it, or shield everyone.
The sulphur elemental, hottest of its line, stokes the others by three and vents by five; a wyvern dives behind the primers.
A duel for one machine: three bites at once strip a shield a Barrier cannot save, or one scorching maul it can. Read which is coming, and mind the heat the maul leaves.
The duel doubled, a fight for two machines: three bites at once strip a shield a Barrier cannot save, or one scorching maul it can. Read which is coming, and mind the heat the maul leaves.
